divisions.text: Called tricks from easier to harder. Land each one within three tries to move up.

divisions.name: Diabolo Freestyle
divisions.text: One diabolo or more. Tell us which when you register.

divisions.name: Spin Top Freestyle
divisions.text: String-thrown or hand-spun tops in a short routine.

divisions.text: Any other toy you can trick with.

divisions.name: Artistic Performance
divisions.text: Any toy. A longer performance judged on artistry, not trick count: choreography, music, and stage presence. Props and costumes welcome.

divisions.name: Showcase
divisions.text: Not a competition. Show the crowd what your toy can do, solo or with friends, at any level.

divisions.name: Beginner (Any Toy)
divisions.text: First contest? Bring any toy and do a short routine to house music.

divisions_notes: Competing in more than one division? Registration is charged per division unless a combo price is listed.
Each toy is judged only against the same toy. Artistic Performance is judged on artistry, so every toy shares it. The Rules page explains how.

gear.title: What to Bring
gear.intro: Bring your own toys, and spares for anything that can break or wear out.
items: Yo-yo and diabolo: spare string already cut to length.
Kendama: a spare string, and tape if you use it.
Spin top: spare strings and closed-toe shoes.
Your music on your phone as a backup, if your division uses your own track.

steps: Name your file DIVISION_LastName_FirstName.mp3, like YY_Park_Jo.mp3.
MP3 format, clean lyrics only. Trim it to your division's routine length.
Send it by {music_deadline}. Bring a backup on your phone.

schedule.title: Check-In & Warm-Up
schedule.text: Registration desk and practice area open.

schedule.title: Showcase
schedule.text: Not judged. Sit back and enjoy.

schedule.title: Awards
schedule.text: Awards for every division and sponsor thanks.

schedule_notes: Times may change on the day based on the number of competitors. Check the registration desk for the running order.

rules.title: Contest Ruleset
rules.intro: Every toy has its own division and is judged only against the same toy, except Artistic Performance, which every toy shares. Freestyles use a typical three-part judging sheet, Artistic Performance uses its own criteria, and the kendama ladder is scored by the tricks you land.

sections.title: Freestyle Format
items: Routine lengths are listed with each division on the Register page.
Your routine starts with the music and ends when the music stops.
Music must be suitable for all ages. No explicit lyrics.
Be ready when you're called. Missing your slot may forfeit your spot.

sections.title: Kendama Ladder
items: Judges call tricks in order, from easier to harder.
You get a set number of attempts per trick, announced at the briefing.
Land the trick to move up. Miss every attempt and your run ends.
Ties are broken by a sudden-death trick.

sections.title: Artistic Performance & Showcase
items: Artistic Performance is judged on the criteria listed on this page, not on trick difficulty alone.
Props, costumes, and partners on stage are fine if they stay inside the stage area and are cleared right after.
Showcase acts are not judged or ranked. Groups of up to six are welcome.
Both use your own music. Send it with your freestyle music.

sections.title: Equipment
items: Bring your own toys. Any brand is welcome.
Check strings before you compete, and replace any that are frayed.
Spin tops: hand-spun or string-launched only. No launchers or motors.
Judges may inspect equipment before you compete.

sections.title: Safety
items: Look before you throw or toss. Keep looping, offstring, and tosses inside the stage area.
Warm up only in the practice area.

sections.title: Judging & Conduct
items: Judge decisions are final.
Respectful conduct is required. Unsportsmanlike behavior may mean disqualification.
Organizers may adjust the format based on registration numbers.

rules.scoring_intro: Each judge scores three categories for every freestyle, comparing you only with players of the same toy. Scores are averaged across the panel.

scoring.title: Difficulty
items: How hard the tricks are, and how many different kinds you show.
Harder combinations and smooth transitions score higher than repeats.

scoring.title: Execution
items: Clean catches, control, and recoveries.
Drops and unplanned stops cost points. Pick it up and keep going.

scoring.title: Performance
items: Use of the stage and connection with the audience.
Musicality: hitting the beats and changes in your song.
Construction: how the routine fits together from start to finish.

scoring_notes: The Artistic Performance criteria and points are a typical starting point, not any organization's official rules. Change them to match your judging sheet.

terms.intro: By registering as a competitor or attending {name} {year}, you agree to these terms. Parents and guardians registering minor competitors agree on their behalf. They cover refunds, assumption of risk, photo release, conduct, and minors.

sections.title: Refund & Cancellation Policy
paragraphs: Registration fees are non-refundable once payment is confirmed, except:
items: Medical emergency: if a documented medical emergency keeps you from competing, email {email} before the contest. We'll consider a full or partial refund.
Duplicate payment: if you're charged twice by mistake, the duplicate charge is refunded in full.
Division cancelled: if we cancel a division and can't move you to another, that division's fee is refunded in full.
after: Other reasons, like schedule conflicts or travel problems, aren't eligible. Fees pay for the venue, equipment, and awards ahead of time.
Registration is personal and can't be transferred to another competitor. To request a refund, email {email} with the subject "Refund Request" as early as you can.

sections.title: Assumption of Risk & Liability Waiver
paragraphs: Skill toy activities carry risks, including contact with thrown, tossed, or spinning equipment, unexpected movement of other participants, and falls. By competing or attending, you accept those risks.
{organizer}, its volunteers, and the venue are not liable for injury, loss, theft, or property damage connected with the contest, to the fullest extent the law allows.
Competitors are responsible for keeping their equipment safe and in working order. Organizers may stop any equipment or performance that puts others at risk.
For minors: a parent or legal guardian must acknowledge this waiver at check-in. Minors can't compete without it.

sections.title: Photo & Video Release
paragraphs: {name} is a public event. It will be photographed, recorded, and may be livestreamed by organizers, media, sponsors, and attendees.

By competing or attending, you consent to being photographed and recorded, and you give {organizer} a non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use those images for contest records, promotion of future events, and club communications. No payment is provided.
Stage routines are recorded for judging and may be shared publicly as part of the contest archive.
Don't want to be photographed? Tell an organizer at check-in. We'll make reasonable efforts, but we can't guarantee you won't appear in photos of a public event.

sections.title: Code of Conduct
paragraphs: Everyone at the contest, including competitors, spectators, volunteers, and staff, is expected to:
items: Treat others with respect, whatever their age, skill level, background, or identity.
Never harass, intimidate, discriminate against, or threaten anyone.
Compete with integrity. Don't interfere with other competitors' performances or equipment.
Follow instructions from contest staff and venue staff.
Keep the competition area and venue clean and safe.
Clear the stage and warm-up space when staff ask.
after: Breaking this code can mean disqualification, removal from the venue, or a ban from future events. The contest director's decisions are final. To report a problem, talk to any staff member or email {email}.

sections.title: Minor Participant Policy
paragraphs: Competitors and spectators of all ages are welcome. For anyone under 18:
items: Registration: a parent or legal guardian must register the competitor and agrees to these terms on their behalf.
Waiver: a parent or guardian must be present at check-in, or have sent written acknowledgment of the waiver, before the minor competes.
Supervision: minors watching the contest should come with a parent or guardian. Organizers aren't responsible for unaccompanied minors.

Names and photos: results for minors are shown as first name and last initial unless a parent opts in to full names. Parents can ask staff at check-in to limit their child's appearance in event media.

sections.title: Event Cancellation
paragraphs: If the contest is cancelled entirely for reasons beyond our control, like severe weather, venue closure, or a public health emergency, competitors get a full refund within 30 days of the announcement.
If the contest changes significantly but still happens (fewer divisions, a new venue), we'll tell competitors as early as possible and work with each person case by case.
